mechanisms.behavior: Four balls occupy switches 18-21 from left to right. Output 1 advances the rightmost ball through jam opto 22 toward shooter lane switch 23. The harness scenarios deliberately seed 18-21 from this proven physical initial state; the seed itself is not treated as a ROM observation.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: Output 2 launches a ball held at shooter-lane switch 23. Preserve the cabinet's manual plunger path as well as ROM-controlled auto launch.
mechanisms.label: Auto launcher and manual plunger

mechanisms.behavior: The four-position vertical mini-trough stacks balls at switches 41, 40, 39, and 38, with jam opto 42 on the exit path. Output 3 fires one ball at a time; multiball release can pulse rapidly enough to eject the stack sequentially.
mechanisms.label: Megatron four-ball mini-trough

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 3 remains active while the Allspark saucer holds a ball. Output 22 ejects it back onto the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Allspark left eject

mechanisms.behavior: Output 5 opens the single controlled orbit gate installed on the Pro. Output 4 is physically unused; the extra left rollover-lane gate is LE-only even though the shared VPX script registers a convenience callback at 4.
mechanisms.label: Right/top orbit control gate

mechanisms.behavior: The ramp normally sits down and feeds a curved lane into the right orbit. Output 30 powers a motor/cam that raises its rear so a fast shot jumps into the Optimus toy; switches 43 and 44 report the fully up and fully down endpoints, and neither endpoint switch should be asserted in transit.
mechanisms.label: Optimus Prime motorized ramp

mechanisms.behavior: A ball jumping from the raised ramp strikes the target in Optimus Prime's left leg at switch 51. The dedicated solenoid under the right foot rocks the figure; it is not a third flipper.
mechanisms.label: Optimus Prime bash toy

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 45 senses the captive ball and switch 1 senses the adjacent Bumblebee standup. The car and captive ball are passive playfield elements without a controller actuator.
mechanisms.label: Bumblebee captive-ball and target area

mechanisms.behavior: Top, right, and bottom pop output/switch pairs are 9/30, 10/31, and 11/32.
mechanisms.label: Three pop bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Left and right slings use output/switch pairs 13/26 and 14/27.
mechanisms.label: Two slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Outputs 15/16 drive the lower left/right flippers. Dedicated public inputs 84/83 are the left button/normally-closed EOS pair and 82/81 are the right pair. No upper or third flipper is installed.
mechanisms.label: Two-flipper assembly

mechanisms.behavior: Each rotation pulse of the passive spinner closes switch 34.
mechanisms.label: Right-orbit spinner

mechanisms.behavior: The Energon targets are 2, 46, and 49; Bumblebee is 1; the right-side two-bank is 37 bottom and 50 top. These are standups, not resettable drop targets.
mechanisms.label: Standup targets and right two-bank

mechanisms.behavior: Switches 4/10 bracket the left ramp, 35 and the edition-specific exit address bracket the right ramp, 5/6 sense the left orbit, 12 the right orbit, 34 its spinner, 7/8 the top lanes, and 11 the center lane. The Optimus ramp changes one upper route but does not replace these sensors.
mechanisms.label: Ramps, orbits, and top lanes

mechanisms.behavior: Output 8 is the optional 16 VAC shaker installation and may be absent from a stock machine.
mechanisms.label: Optional shaker motor

physical.notes: The official Pro chart leaves Q4 unused. The proven VPX script registers a left-gate callback for shared table code, but physical review confirms that second controlled gate is LE-only.
The edition-specific service chart is authoritative: LE powers this optional Q24 circuit from ORG/J16-P4 at 20 VDC, while the Pro supplement specifies RED/J16-P4-8 at 5 VDC.
PinMAME's SAM_FASTFLIPSOL synthetic output. It gates low-latency flipper handling and is not a physical I/O Power Driver transistor.
